root_idea.summary: The root centers on throwing, casting, or projecting something away or toward a target, with force or distance often salient.
root_idea.development: The physical image extends to casting abstract things into hearts or against falsehood, uttering conjectures, verbal disparagement, and nouns for projectiles and throwing instruments. The lexical record also develops related ideas of remoteness, rapid movement, ejection, and mountain flanks.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form قَذَفَ.

senses.definition: To throw, cast, or project a person or thing away, into a place, or toward a target.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic physical uses include casting into a place, throwing an object, and being pelted or hurled in the passive. The verb may occur in imperative, perfect, imperfect, active, or passive forms without creating separate lexical senses.

senses.definition: To cast an abstract thing into a recipient or upon an opposing object, especially to cast terror into hearts or truth upon falsehood.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a figurative projection construction: an abstract content is made to reach or confront a target, as with terror cast into hearts and truth cast upon falsehood.

senses.definition: To utter conjectures about what is hidden or not established.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the construction بِالْغَيْبِ for speaking speculatively about the unseen or concealed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To revile, reproach, asperse, defame, or give someone a bad name.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use for verbal disparagement, also expressed as casting something at a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To charge a woman with adultery.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The recorded construction applies to charging a chaste, honest, or married woman with adultery.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reproach or accuse someone of a matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with بِهِ to charge a person with the matter represented by the attached pronoun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause something to reach or strike someone; to afflict someone with it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded as equivalent to أَصَابَهُ بِهِ, distinct from merely naming or accusing someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To shoot or propel an arrow.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded in the expression قُذِفَتْ بِاللَّحْمِ, said of a camel and treated in the evidence as a tropical expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land in which there is no pasture where cattle may freely range.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal description of uncultivable or pastureless land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A catapult or mangonel, an instrument for throwing something a great distance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for a throwing machine.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A town or place that is far away or remote.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive adjective applied to a distant town or place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Remote or far away, said of a dwelling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Both قَذَفٌ and قَذِيفٌ are recorded as descriptions of a distant dwelling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Speed of travel or rapid progress.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun describing swiftness of movement.
The description evokes a horse that seems to throw itself forward in its running.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sides or outlying portions of a mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The singular is given as قَذَفٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing thrown or projected; a projectile.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the object cast or hurled.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To vomit or eject what is in the stomach.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate Classical use explained through the image of throwing something out.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Physical throwing of stones and other objects.
Physical casting and figurative casting of speech or light.
General verbal defamation and defamation involving a chaste woman.
Reproaching or accusing someone of a matter.
Causing something to reach or strike someone.

cautions: Lane's historical Quran citations are not converted into modern verse keys; the Quran examples use the independently supplied QAC locations.
The camel-fattening expression is marked as an assumed tropical usage in the supplied lexical evidence.
The remote, swift-movement, mountain-side, projectile, and vomiting branches are recorded as broader Classical or root-level lexical evidence, not as additional Quranic form groups.
